stem:
Meena is learning how breathing works in our body. Air reaches tiny air sacs called alveoli in the lungs, which are surrounded by thin blood vessels.
What happens at the alveoli during gas exchange?

options.text: Carbon dioxide passes from the alveoli into the blood and oxygen passes from the blood into the alveoli
Oxygen passes from the alveoli into the blood and carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the alveoli
The alveoli transfer oxygen into the blood only when no blood vessels surround them
Fresh air flows directly from the alveoli into the blood vessels as a whole

teacher.key_rationale: At the alveoli, oxygen diffuses from the alveolar air into the surrounding blood while carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood into the alveoli to be exhaled. Option B states this correctly; A reverses the gases, C omits the blood-vessel condition, and D conflates airflow with diffusion.
